Definition: from G1722 and G1391; in glory, i.e. splendid, (figuratively) noble:--glorious, gorgeous(-ly), honourable.
BiblicalUsage: Endoxos is what is glorious, splendid, honourable. The apostles were despised while the Corinthians were honourable in 1 Corinthians 4:10, Christ will present His church glorious, without spot or wrinkle, in Ephesians 5:27, and the people rejoiced for all the glorious things Jesus did in Luke 13:17. The word also dresses kings' courts, where men live gorgeously apparelled in Luke 7:25.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe true glory is not the court's gorgeously apparelled life but a church without spot, presented to Christ. I hold that the honour the world gives fades, but the glory Christ gives His people lasts — and I would rather be despised with the apostles than honoured without Him.
